_note: Verified patches to installed third-party skills. Arming runs `patch-skills.mjs apply` after every install, so a reinstall is repaired instead of silently erasing the fix. Each patch is an exact unified diff with context: if upstream moves, `check` reports drift and `apply` refuses rather than guessing. `required` follows the pack's tier — a missing core skill is an error, a missing optional skill is skipped.
_requires: git on PATH (`git apply` is the patch engine); no network and no other dependency.

patches.why: `spawn("agy")` resolves only through PATH, but the Antigravity installer writes the User PATH — which a process started before the install, or one inheriting only the Machine PATH, never sees. The relay then reports `agy_unavailable (exit 127)` although the binary is present and working. PATH is still tried first; the fallback checks the documented install locations and is consulted only when a plain spawn would fail.

result.json reported the flags the caller ASKED for, not the ones agy ran with. A read-only run passes `--sandbox --dangerously-skip-permissions` itself, so every read-only lane reported `sandbox: false, dangerouslySkipPermissions: false` while agy ran with both — a reader could not tell what the run was allowed to do. The header's sandbox guarantee was also stated as fact although it was measured on macOS only: on agy 1.4.4 / Windows `--sandbox` confines nothing, and writes persisted inside and outside the workspace. The result now carries `effectivePosture` (the flags, the platform, and whether they were enforced) and `effectiveArgv` (what agy was actually given); the header names the platform each claim was measured on.

result.json reported `auto: opts.auto` — the REQUESTED flag — but --auto is never passed on a plan (read-only) run, because it would auto-approve the plan agent's ask-gated edit/bash permissions and let a `--read-only` review modify the tree. So a plan run reported `auto: true` while running with no --auto at all. The result now carries `auto` as the EFFECTIVE value (`opts.auto && agent !== 'plan'`), plus `effectivePosture` (auto, agent, plan, requestedAuto) and `effectiveArgv` (what opencode was actually given).

Cleanup must never be the thing that fails. On Windows a relay killed from outside leaves a child holding the temporary snapshot, and `rmSync` throws EPERM — masking whatever actually went wrong. The patch retries five times for the handles to drop, then names the directory and returns instead of throwing. An orphaned temp dir is harmless; a misleading EPERM is not.

A judge that writes is not a judge. debate-review runs its reviewers read-only, but dispatch.mjs only LOGGED a WARNING when the relay reported readOnlyViolation: true — the run still returned success and the diff could be landed. The patch turns the WARNING into a thrown error so the review fails loudly and the orchestrator bounces or escalates instead of shipping a review that touched the tree.

Three defects measured on win32 with agent-browser 0.39.1. (a) The version gate treated anything newer than 0.32.x as a warning, so 0.39.x passed preflight and returned broken evidence; the patch separates a hard floor from the verified contract. (b) The recorder cannot finalize — `record stop` writes a zero-byte file and `record start` can hang — so capture is skipped and `completeness.video` reads "missing" with a `videoReason`, instead of shipping an unplayable artifact. (c) `spawnSync` cannot execute the npm .cmd/.ps1 shim on Windows, so the CLI is resolved to its native .exe. `references/formats.md` documents `videoReason`.
